issues.description: Method name mismatch for Stock.emptyStock(): The problem statement UML and the solution repository define a Stock method named emptyStock() returning void, but the template repository's Stock class defines a method named clearInventory() instead. This naming inconsistency means students reading the spec or solution will expect Stock.emptyStock(), while the starter code exposes clearInventory(), which can confuse students and cause API mismatches when they try to call or implement emptyStock().
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template API match the problem statement and solution by renaming the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock(), preserving the implementation. Alternatively, add a new public void emptyStock() method in the template that delegates to clearInventory() (e.g., public void emptyStock() { clearInventory(); }) so both names are available and students can follow the specification.

issues.description: Identifier naming mismatch for the operation that clears the stock inventory: the problem statement (UML) specifies a Stock.emptyStock() method, the solution repository implements Stock.emptyStock(), but the template repository provides a method named Stock.clearInventory(). A student reading the problem will look for or attempt to implement emptyStock() while the template already contains clearInventory(), causing confusion about which method to modify or call and increasing mapping effort between requirements and template code.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier for the stock-clearing operation across all artifacts. Either rename the template method clearInventory() to emptyStock() so it matches the problem statement and solution, or update the problem statement/UML and the solution to reference clearInventory() instead. Ensure all references (documentation, tests, and code) use the same name (preferred: emptyStock()) so students can directly map the requirement to the template implementation.
